editorial.headline: Textile Household Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Specialist retail in household textiles is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s risk-based PMA moratorium blocks registration there.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register a PMA business under this activity in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact, even though the national setting is open and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA where the risk classification is Low or Medium-Low. Here, every stated scope at the Large scale is assessed Low/Medium-Low, bringing the activity within that moratorium. Its Bali status is recorded as blocked by risk class, with the cited moratorium from May 2026.

The activity itself is specialist retail in textile household supplies. Its scope runs from tablecloths and bed sheets to tarpaulins, pillowcases, mosquito nets, mattress fabrics and pillow fabrics. Mop cloths and household linen sit within the same retail scope, alongside pillows and bolsters. What connects these goods is their place in equipping and maintaining the home: practical textiles for everyday use, as well as the soft goods used across household spaces.

Scale does not narrow the national coverage. The record opens the activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses, giving the same national classification to retailers operating at very different sizes. It also makes clear that foreign participation is not subject to a national ownership ceiling below full ownership: the ceiling is 100%. The listed national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. National openness is therefore real, but it is not a substitute for the Bali position where the local moratorium applies.

The accurate reading keeps those two levels separate. Nationally, this is an open activity across all four stated scales, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, the result is not a lower percentage or a conditional route; it is a PMA registration block because the Large-scale risk outcome across the stated scopes is Low/Medium-Low. For anyone considering this retail activity in Bali, that local restriction is the controlling position.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is real, but in Bali the Low/Medium-Low risk outcome produces a direct PMA registration block.
